classification.difficultyReason: Draw two north-based bearing legs, identify and add their eastward components, and retain exact special-angle values.

content.prompt: A ship travels from $P$ to $Q$ on a bearing of $060^\circ$ for 40 km and from $Q$ to $R$ on a bearing of $045^\circ$ for 25 km. Draw a clear diagram using this information and find how far east of $P$ $R$ is, in km. Give your answer in exact form.

answer.short:
$\left(20\sqrt3+\frac{25\sqrt2}{2}\right)\text{ km}$.

Add the eastward components of the two legs.
answer.worked:
The bearings are measured clockwise from north, so each eastward component is the distance multiplied by the sine of its bearing.
$$\begin{align*}E_{PQ}&=40\sin60^\circ\\E_{PQ}&=20\sqrt3\text{ km}\\E_{QR}&=25\sin45^\circ\\E_{QR}&=\frac{25\sqrt2}{2}\text{ km}\\E_{PR}&=20\sqrt3+\frac{25\sqrt2}{2}\text{ km}\end{align*}$$
Thus $R$ is $\left(20\sqrt3+\frac{25\sqrt2}{2}\right)\text{ km}$ east of $P$.
